name: Underwriting Review
description: Referral raised by flow 1 (underwriting-evaluate) when the 41-rule engine returns REFER. Review the submission, the referral reasons and the interim premium, then move this task to Approved or Declined — flow 11 (referral-decide) reads that move and writes decision_config accordingly. Do not tick the form action and leave the task open: the underwriter's own status move is what flow 11 watches, not the action.

task_actions.description: Record the referral decision — outcome, reasons and premium breakdown

_notes.priority_and_tag: Both copied verbatim from contract artefact 4 (04-status-vocabulary.json): priority `high` and tag `referral` are what flow 1 writes on this task kind. The `referral` tag is flow 11's mandatory gate — omitting it here would make a task seeded from this template invisible to flow 11 even after an underwriter approves it.
_notes.form_action: Pinned to decision_config with no named view (empty `view` = the config's default view, per TaskTemplateActionConfig's doc comment in workspaces-service/model/api.go:325-334). decision_config has only a `table` view at time of writing (verified by reading record_configs/decision_config.json, not edited) — no dedicated 'underwriter' view exists yet to pin to. Leaving `view` unset is forward-compatible: whichever wave adds decision_config's form view, this template resolves it without a coordinated rename. This differs from the Void Override template below, which DOES pin a view, because that one is the plan's stated required-field mechanism and cannot be left to resolve itself.
_notes.status_and_A4-1: Contract artefact 4's open ambiguity A4-1 leaves 'does this task carry a form action at all' explicitly undecided and safe either way. This template includes one because §6.4 and recon-c build item 5 both ask for it, and because the space's `closed` status (role: done) absorbs the platform's status-reset side effect of seeding a task action at creation time (AddTaskActionHandler -> updateTaskStatusFromActions), which lands back on `open` here since ANTIPODEAN declares no `todo` role and default_status is `open` — a harmless no-op only because the action is seeded at creation, never added to an already-worked task (status_write_prohibitions #2 in artefact 4).
_notes.assignees: Deliberately left unset. The account's only listed users (via list_users) are demo/test accounts belonging to other verticals (FAHUB client folders, admin demo logins) — none represent a real Antipodean underwriter, compliance, claims or finance user. Hardcoding one of those ids as a default assignee would misroute work. Assignment happens at task-creation/instantiation time by whoever is doing the work.
